voices.note: the תנו רבנן at 18a.10 on carrying bones

props.gloss_en: one who carries bones from place to place may not put them in a saddlebag, set them on a donkey's back and ride on them
and if he was afraid of gentiles or of bandits -- it is permitted
and as they said of bones, so they said of a Torah scroll
(entertained) the comparison refers to the first clause: a Torah scroll, like bones, may not be ridden on
rather, the comparison refers to the latter clause: the permission in fear of gentiles or bandits

schemas.gloss_en: מי גרע ספר תורה מעצמות? -- is a Torah scroll inferior to bones? what may not be done to bones surely may not be done to a Torah scroll

frames.gloss_en: אהייא? -- to which clause of the baraita does 'so they said of a Torah scroll' refer?
frames.exhaustive_gloss: the baraita has two clauses, and אהייא? אילימא ארישא... אלא אסיפא runs through both

alternatives.gloss_en: the survivor: the latter clause -- the permission in fear
the rival: the first clause -- the prohibition

eliminated_by.gloss_en: פשיטא! מי גרע ספר תורה מעצמות? -- that would be obvious: a Torah scroll is no less than bones, so the baraita would be teaching nothing
